8. Whittaker modules

In Sections 6 and 7, we gave examples of $\mathcal{D}_{t}$ -modules with a Lie group action that was compatible with the $\mathcal{D}_{t}$ -module structure77
7

Compatible in the sense that the differential of the group action agrees with the Lie algebra action coming from $\mathcal{D}_{t}$ .. These were examples of Harish-Chandra sheaves. In this section, we will give another example of a $\mathcal{D}_{t}$ -module with a Lie group action, but now the two actions will differ by a character of the Lie algebra. This is an example of a twisted Harish-Chandra sheaf. Twisted Harish-Chandra sheaves first arose in [HMSW87, Appendix B] in the study of Harish-Chandra modules for semisimple Lie groups with infinite center, and were later used in [MS14] to provide a geometric description of Whittaker modules.

Let $N$ be as in Section 6 and $\mathfrak{n}=\Lie{N}$ . Fix a Lie algebra morphism $\eta:\mathfrak{n}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ . Because $\mathfrak{n}$ is spanned by the matrix $E$ , this morphism is determined by the image of $E$ , which we will also refer to as $\eta$ :

$\eta:=\eta(E)\in\mathbb{C}.$

Our starting place is the $\eta$ -twisted connection $\mathcal{O}_{U_{\infty},\eta}$ . As a sheaf of rings on $U_{\infty}$ ,

$\mathcal{O}_{U_{\infty},\eta}=\mathcal{O}_{U_{\infty}},$

but the $\mathcal{D}_{U_{\infty}}$ -module structure is twisted by $\eta$ . It suffices to describe this $\mathcal{D}_{U_{\infty}}$ -module structure on global sections as $U_{\infty}$ is affine. The $D(U_{\infty})$ -action on the vector space $\mathcal{O}_{U_{\infty},\eta}(U_{\infty})=\mathbb{C}[w]$ is given by

(8.1)

$\partial_{w}\cdot w^{k}=kw^{k-1}-\eta w^{k},\hskip 5.69054ptw\cdot w^{k}=w^{k+1}.$

paper.title: Four examples of Beilinson-Bernstein localization
paper.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra. The Beilinson-Bernstein localization theorem establishes an equivalence of the category of $\mathfrak{g}$-modules of a fixed infinitesimal character and a category of modules over a twisted sheaf of differential operators on the flag variety of $\mathfrak{g}$. In this expository paper, we give four detailed examples of this theorem when $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})$. Specifically, we describe the $\mathcal{D}$-modules associated to finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathfrak{g}$-modules, Verma modules, Whittaker modules, discrete series representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$, and principal series representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$.
